q-90387.name: Question 1
q-90387.problem:
Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\text{E}[X].$

$$
f(x)=\frac{{x}^{3}}{4},\,0\le x\le 2
$$
q-90387.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the expected value using the following formula:

$$
\text{E}[X]={\int }_{S}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x
$$

 

We compute the expected value of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{0}^{2}x\cdot \frac{{x}^{3}}{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{5}}{20}|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{8}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
f(x)=\frac{6}{7}(3x-{x}^{2}),\,0\le x\le 1

q-130872.name: Question 8
q-130872.problem:
Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\text{E}[X].$

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{6x}{5}, & 0<x<1 \\ \frac{2}{5x}, & 1\le x<e\end{aligned}
$$
q-130872.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the expected value using the following formula:

$$
\text{E}[X]={\int }_{S}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x
$$

 

We compute the expected value of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{0}^{e}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{e}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\cdot \frac{6x}{5}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{e}x\cdot \frac{2}{5x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{6{x}^{2}}{5}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{2}{5}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{2{x}^{3}}{5}|}_{0}^{1}+{\frac{2x}{5}|}_{1}^{e} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}+\frac{2e}{5}-\frac{2}{5} \\  & =\frac{2e}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

$$

q-152902.problem:
Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\text{E}[4X-3].$

$$
f(x)=\frac{3}{{x}^{4}},\,1\le x
$$
q-152902.worked_solution:
First, we simplify using the properties of expected value:

$$
\text{E}[4X-3]=4\text{E}[X]-3
$$

For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the expected value using the following formula:

$$
\text{E}[X]={\int }_{S}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, we calculate the expected value of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{S}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }x\cdot \frac{3}{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{3}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={-\frac{3}{2{x}^{2}}|}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[4X-3] & =4\text{E}[X]-3 \\  & =4\cdot \frac{3}{2}-3 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

First, we simplify using the properties of the expected value:

$$
\text{E}[4X+2]=4\text{E}[X]+2
$$

For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the expected value using the following formula:

$$
\text{E}[X]={\int }_{S}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, we calculate the expected value of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\cdot \frac{3}{4}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }x\cdot \frac{1}{2{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3x}{4}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{3{x}^{2}}{8})|}_{0}^{1}+{(-\frac{1}{2x})|}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =(\frac{3}{8}-0)+(0-(-\frac{1}{2})) \\  & =\frac{3}{8}+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{7}{8}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[4X+2] & =4\text{E}[X]+2 \\  & =4\cdot \frac{7}{8}+2 \\  & =\frac{11}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
